name: Jubilant Agri and Consumer Products Ltd (JACPL)
tagline: A genuinely high-ROCE Jubilant-group niche polymer/adhesives-plus-fertilizer business mid-way through an active NCLT demerger, but the community's own SOTP math says the immediate arb upside is modest, not a screaming special situation
business_overview: JACPL (Jubilant Bhartia Group) runs three segments: Performance Polymers & Chemicals (VP-latex — India's largest producer, used in tyre-cord dipping; SPVA/ester gum — among global top-2, sold to chewing-gum makers), Consumer Adhesives/Wood Finishes (Jivanjor, Charmwood, competing against Pidilite's ~70% market share), and P&K Fertilizers (Ramban-brand SSP, ~4.44 lakh TPA, North India) plus specialty Agri-Nutrients. Demerged from Jubilant Industries Ltd in FY24 via slump sale; now itself mid-process of demerging the Agri/Sulphuric-Acid business into a separate entity (Jubilant Agri Solutions Ltd) — an NCLT-directed creditors' meeting on the scheme was scheduled for 5-Sep-2026.
fundamentals_table: Rs 2,807 Cr (screener) / Rs 2,353-3,556 Cr cited across the thread at different dates as the price moved
ROCE ~32-37%, ROE ~30-31% (FY25) — well above fertilizer/adhesive peer averages
5yr revenue CAGR ~25% (Rs622cr FY21 to Rs1,541cr FY25), but lumpy (TTM shows -15% de-growth per one snapshot); FY25 EBITDA ~Rs146cr, PAT Rs88.2cr
D/E ~5%; gross borrowings fell Rs162cr (Mar-24) to Rs77cr (Mar-25), Net Debt/EBITDA <1x, down from Debt/EBITDA 5.5x in FY19
JACPL ~26-27x P/E vs Pidilite ~75x (ROE 23%), SRF ~68x (ROE 10%), Coromandel ~38x (ROE 17.5%) — cheap on a return-adjusted peer basis
fundamentals_narrative: A genuinely high-quality, deleveraging, high-ROCE business (32-37% ROCE, D/E ~5%) trading at a peer-relative discount (26x P/E for 31% ROE vs Pidilite's 75x for 23% ROE) — the 'hidden gem' framing is fundamentally supported. But two independent, quantified community SOTP analyses (Oct-2025 and Mar-2026) both concluded the demerger-specific arbitrage upside from current prices is modest (~17-20%), not the outsized special-situations gap the thread's title suggests — a genuinely useful corrective to the initiating post's more bullish framing.

Arc: a comprehensive trusted initiating overview -> a follow-up flagging the adhesive segment's underwhelming growth -> a detailed SOTP-based demerger analysis (comfort threshold not met at current price) -> a further SOTP check reaching a similar 'not super attractive' conclusion -> a Sep-2026 one-line AGM-attendance query with no answer yet.

Niral_Maru (not trusted) separately flagged that the adhesive business specifically 'is not really picking up steam' despite phenomenal Q1 results elsewhere.
bse_notes: Folok flagged that related-party transactions with sister Jubilant-group companies (Ingrevia, Pharmova) warrant due diligence (FY25 AR p.223) — a governance item worth independent verification, not addressed further in-thread.
bull_case: Genuinely high, improving return ratios (ROCE 32-37%, ROE ~31%) with debt falling sharply (Debt/EBITDA 5.5x FY19 to <1x now) — a real quality improvement, not just a story

Niche B2B technical moats in two segments: India's largest VP-latex producer (tyre-cord dipping) and among global top-2 in SPVA/ester gum (chewing-gum base) — genuine technical barriers, not commodity positions
Trades at a real peer-relative discount: ~26-27x P/E for 31% ROE vs Pidilite's ~75x for 23% ROE or SRF's ~68x for 10% ROE

Active, real demerger process (NCLT creditors' meeting scheduled 5-Sep-2026) separating the subsidy-dependent, margin-dilutive fertilizer business from the higher-quality polymers/adhesives franchise — a genuine, dated catalyst, not a vague ambition
Adhesive brand Jivanjor is gaining share faster than both Pidilite and a key mid-tier peer (17% vs 10%/8% growth) — a real top-line signal even if the margin implication is unresolved
bear_case: Two independent, carefully quantified community SOTP analyses both concluded the immediate demerger-arbitrage upside is only ~17-20% at then-current prices — well short of the ~50% margin-of-safety threshold either poster wanted for a special-situations entry; the 'hidden gem' framing is a quality/valuation thesis more than a demerger-arb thesis

Consumer-adhesives segment carries a genuine unresolved question: 9% operating margin vs 20%+ for peers while gaining share — could be a weak brand buying volume via discounts/dealer incentives just as plausibly as a strong brand reinvesting in growth, and no one in-thread has resolved which

Real information-access constraint: no concalls and thin recent rating-agency coverage, per a direct community observation — makes independent verification of the demerger timeline and segment economics harder than for a typical mainboard mid-cap

Fertilizer segment remains structurally subsidy/policy-dependent with genuine margin volatility (the very reason for the demerger) and RPT with sister Jubilant-group entities warrants due diligence that hasn't been done in-thread

four_box.note: Tailwind yes: an active, dated demerger process (NCLT creditors' meeting 5-Sep-2026) separating the higher-quality polymers/adhesives business from the subsidy-dependent fertilizer drag. TAM weak: VP-latex/SPVA niches are real but modest in absolute size, and the adhesives segment faces Pidilite's ~70% share dominance with an unresolved margin-quality question. Moat yes: India's-largest VP-latex + global-top-2 SPVA positions are genuine B2B technical-barrier moats, not marketing claims. Valuation yes: 26-27x P/E for 31% ROE is genuinely cheap versus every cited peer, independently corroborated by the trusted initiating post's own peer table.

value_chain.theme: Niche B2B specialty-polymer supply chains (tyre-cord reinforcement, chewing-gum base) — not a current active_themes.json entry, added because the deep read made the chain position clear
value_chain.position: India's largest VP-latex producer (tyre-cord dipping/reinforcement input for tyre and tyre-fabric manufacturers) and among the global top-2 producers of SPVA/ester gum (the chewy-backbone/binding input for chewing-gum and bubble-gum manufacturers), plus a regional #1 SSP fertilizer brand (Ramban) in UP/Uttarakhand.
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Technical/quality-certification barriers in specialty latex grades (VP) and food-grade polymer specs (SPVA/ester gum) — few dedicated global producers in either niche, unlike commodity SBR latex.
value_chain.note: The polymer/latex value-chain position (VP-latex, SPVA) is the genuine technical moat; the adhesives-segment position is structurally weaker (challenger brand against Pidilite's dominant share) and the fertilizer position is a regional-scale commodity play subject to subsidy policy, not a chain bottleneck.
